Hi Vivek / Redwood team,

We're kicking off procurement for a private deployment of Redwood in our on-prem enclave and would like a technical review of the Terraform/Helm/Ansible bundles you propose. Key asks from our side:

Adding the technical checklist details here so Jordan's team can prep. I've pasted the relevant sections from our checklist and included examples for GitLab CI (we use GitLab for Dedicated/Private customers but will adapt if you run another system).

-- Module ownership table (example) --
- redwood-enclave-terraform — owned by infra-modules (team: infra-core), code owners: @infra-core, release: signed terraform module tarball
- redwood-helm-edge-proxy — owned by runtime-team, chart must be semver-tagged + signed
- ansible-enclave-bootstrap — owned by ops-automation, must support httpproxy/env var overrides for air-gapped installs

-- CI gating (required checks before merge to main) --
- terraform fmt + validate (automated)
- terraform plan with policy checks (sent to MR comment)
- helm lint + schema-validation (values.schema.json in repo)
- smoke e2e against a disposable emulator (k3s) for major releases
- artifact signing step: uses cosign to sign container images and helm charts

Example snippet (GitLab stages):
- lint -> plan -> policy-check -> build -> sign -> publish -> canary-deploy -> promote

-- Provenance & supply chain --
We require:
- signed releases (cosign / sigstore)
- supply-chain provenance artifact (SLSA attestation) attached to release metadata

-- Air-gap considerations --
- Ansible must support an offline artifact bundle (tarball) + local registries
- TLS cert distribution: provide an Ansible role to rotate certs and place in trusted CA store
- Drift detection: run a reconciliation job nightly that emits findings to a central S3-like bucket (or an on-prem ELK sink)

Jordan: please confirm whether you need the Ansible role to handle your internal cert-proxy and whether your team prefers rsync or OCI registry pull for images. I'm attaching a short pipeline example (gitlab-pipeline-examples.yml).

— Mina
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: gitlab-pipeline-examples.yml (CI snippets)

Thanks both — that checklist is exactly the kind of detail we need. A few notes from our side:

- We run GitLab EE on-prem and prefer OCI registry pulls to rsync for image delivery; we'll provide a private registry endpoint.
- Air-gap: we require support for a TLS intercepting proxy that injects a client cert for outbound artifact pulls. The Ansible role must be able to configure the proxy and pin certs.
- Network: our diagram uses private egress via a NAT with strict NACLs — we need a short list of required outbound ports (e.g., cosign, time sync, OCSP) so our network/security team can pre-approve.

I've uploaded our network diagram to our share (link below) and attached a small ZIP of our current registry TLS config. Please add a short preflight checklist item for required outbound ports.

Jordan
